title: Forex market participants can profit in both uptrends and downtrends through long and short positions
claim: Traders can generate profit regardless of market direction by going long (buying) or short (selling)

source.section: Making Money in Up and Down Markets

support: Explicit coverage of bull markets and shorting mechanics
mechanism: Directional bias + position management
validation: Requires historical trade records

title: Successful trading requires systematic analysis discipline, not day-to-day chart watching
claim: Treating trading as a professional discipline with structured analysis methods outperforms reactive chart-watching behavior
support: Book emphasizes employee mindset vs. chart junkie confessions
mechanism: Structured process + discipline + emotional control
validation: Compare win rate / Sharpe under disciplined vs. discretionary execution

title: Multi-timeframe analysis requires examining trend (higher TF) and entries (lower TF)
claim: Traders should identify trend on longer timeframes and trade entries on shorter timeframes for alignment
support: Explicit guidance on timeframe hierarchy
mechanism: Macro trend context + micro entry signal = higher probability
assumptions: Lower TF signals are more timely
validation: Compare single-TF vs. multi-TF entry win rates

title: Markets cycle through sinking, soaring, and sideways phases
claim: Market behavior exhibits repetitive cycles: downtrend (sinking), uptrend (soaring), and range (sideways)
support: Explicit categorization of three market states
mechanism: Cyclical price behavior based on supply/demand dynamics
validation: Statistical analysis of cycle durations and transitions

title: Market memory: price respects previous support/resistance levels
claim: Price levels where prior reversal occurred act as psychological and technical anchors that current price respects
support: Support and resistance concept rooted in repeated price action
mechanism: Order clustering at prior turning points + herd behavior
assumptions: Traders recall and trade from memory levels
validation: Backtest: do reversals cluster near prior highs/lows?

title: Stop loss placement is critical to objective risk control
claim: Stop losses must be placed at technical levels (not arbitrary distance) to avoid whipsaw and ensure defined risk per trade
support: Emphasis on technical placement vs. emotional stops
mechanism: Stop at support/resistance = natural stop, fewer false stops
failure_modes: Stop too wide increases max loss
validation: Backtest with stop-loss rules

title: 2% risk rule: Never risk more than 2% of account per trade
claim: Position sizing should ensure no single trade risk exceeds 2% of total account equity
support: Explicit guidance on position sizing rule
mechanism: Controls max drawdown, preserves capital for recovery
failure_modes: Breakeven after large drawdown takes many trades
Opportunity cost if stops are too tight
validation: Monte Carlo sim with random trade sequences

title: Use objective indicators and trendlines, not subjective indicators, for entries
claim: Order entry should rely on price-based trendlines and support/resistance, not lagging indicators
support: Criticism of subjective indicator interpretation
mechanism: Price-based signals lead entries vs. indicators lag
assumptions: Trendlines are more timely than indicators
failure_modes: Indicator crosses can still work in certain regimes
validation: Win rate comparison

title: Fibonacci levels act as confluence zones for support, resistance, and entry confirmation
claim: Price respects Fibonacci retracements (38.2%, 50%, 61.8%) as support/resistance; confluence with price action improves confidence
support: Detailed examples of Fibonacci in price analysis
mechanism: Psychological levels + order clustering at Fib ratios
validation: Win rate at Fib vs. non-Fib levels

title: Three primary entry setups: Momentum, Swing, and Short Cycle
claim: Momentum trades enter at breakout on higher TF; Swing trades enter on pullback to support; Short Cycle trades exploit range reversals
support: Explicit categorization and description of three setup types
mechanism: Each setup targets different market regime
assumptions: All three setups have positive expectancy
validation: Win rate and Sharpe per setup type

title: Momentum trades: Buy breakouts above resistance; target is 2x the setup range
claim: When price breaks above prior resistance on volume/momentum, enter long; target profit around 2x the setup swing range
support: Specific setup rules for momentum entries
mechanism: Breakout continuation + mean reversion to 2x range
validation: Win rate and Sharpe on momentum trades

title: Swing trades: Buy pullback to support in uptrend; sell pullback to resistance in downtrend
claim: Enter when price retraces 38.2%-50% in the direction of the trend; target is the prior trend high/low
support: Swing setup described with specific entry/exit levels
mechanism: Trend continuation + pullback recovery
validation: Win rate on swing setups

title: Forex trading activity and volatility concentrates during London and New York sessions
claim: Peak FX volume and pip movement occur during London (08:00-17:00 GMT) and New York (13:00-22:00 GMT) sessions; other times are quieter

source.section: FINANCIAL CENTERS YOU NEED TO KNOW & PRIME TIME

support: Detailed session timing and activity levels
mechanism: Market-making concentration + institutional order flow
assumptions: Traders can access/execute during prime sessions
validation: Volatility and volume stats by session

title: Time zone and trading hours constrain live FX execution windows; must account for sleep/availability
claim: Traders with 5-hour/week constraint must plan trading time around work/sleep and select sessions with high edge probability
support: Book emphasizes part-time trader constraints
mechanism: Part-time must exploit best opportunities during available hours
assumptions: Selective execution beats trying all times
validation: Win rate and Sharpe by time zone

title: US Dollar Index correlates with major FX pairs; tracks broad dollar strength/weakness
claim: USD/CAD and AUD/USD exhibit inverse correlation to broad USD strength; observing Dollar Index helps anticipate cross-pair moves
support: Detailed correlation analysis and examples
mechanism: Common fundamental driver (risk appetite, yields, inflation) affects all USD pairs
validation: Correlation stats and rolling windows

title: News releases can trigger sharp price spikes and reversals; trading news is high-risk for small accounts
claim: Major economic news (NFP, Fed decisions, GDP) creates slippage risk and gap risk; book recommends staying flat during major news
support: Explicit warning about news volatility
mechanism: Large institutional orders, risk-on/risk-off, slippage on thin liquidity
assumptions: News impact is large and unpredictable
failure_modes: Trader takes news trade and hits slippage

title: 200-period simple moving average acts as psychological support/resistance across FX pairs
claim: Price respects 200 SMA as a key trend line; breakout above/below 200 SMA often signals trend reversal
support: 200 SMA identified as key moving average level
mechanism: Herd psychology + order clustering near round MA
failure_modes: Too many traders use same MA
validation: Win rate above/below 200 SMA

title: 52-week highs and lows serve as psychological reversal points
claim: Price approaching or breaking 52-week extremes often reverses; these levels trigger stop-runs and profit-taking
support: 52-week extremes identified as key reversal zones
mechanism: Year-high/low triggers momentum traders and stop-runs
validation: Reversal frequency and amplitude at 52W extremes

title: Right side of the chart (most recent price action) provides best entry signals; avoid fading old support
claim: Focus on current price structure vs. old historical levels; recent breakouts and structure are more reliable than old support retest

source.section: THE RIGHT SIDE OF THE CHART

support: Emphasis on recent price action over historical
mechanism: Recent structure reflects current participants; old levels may be stale
assumptions: Current structure is more relevant than history
failure_modes: Recent structure breaks to old support
validation: Compare win rate for recent vs. historical support entries

title: Broker choice affects trading costs (spreads), slippage, and stop-loss execution reliability
claim: Traders must evaluate brokers on spread tightness, stop-loss reliability, and execution speed; poor broker can erase edge

source.section: Is My Broker Friend or Foe?

support: Broker evaluation framework provided
mechanism: Spread + slippage + stop reliability = transaction cost drag
assumptions: Retail broker conflict of interest exists
validation: Backtest with real broker spreads and slippage

title: Charting tools and profit target automation reduce emotional override and execution errors
claim: Setting alerts and profit targets in advance prevents impulsive exits early and ensures discipline
support: Automation discussed as discipline enforcement tool
mechanism: Pre-set levels remove emotion from exit decision
validation: Win rate and Sharpe with fixed targets vs. discretionary
